narr: A series of upper-level short waves moved across the region in persistent, southwesterly upper-level flow combined with moderate instability and shear to produce several rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms across north and central Georgia. Some of these storms dumped 2 to 4 inches of rain over the area, resulting in isolated flash flooding.
ev: The public reported water over the roadway at the intersection of Corinth Road and Millard Farmer Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain accumulated quickly, causing the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Benson Lake Road closed at Mt. Moriah Road due to flooding. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported Puckett Road at Pumpkinvine Creek is flooded. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the quick rise of the creek.

The Emergency Manager reported Sleepy Hollow Road at Brownsville Road was closed due to water over the roadway. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported a road washed out near Line Creek Road and Blanton Mill Road due to high water on the Flint River and Flat Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported water from Mud Creek was covering Honeysuckle Lane. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported water from Lick Log Creek covering Garmon Road and Hunters Mill Drive. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported water from Mud Creek covering the roadway near the intersection of Mudd Creek Road and McGarity Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Winn Road was impassable between Bobby Austin Road and South Paulding High School due to high water from a Sweetwater Creek tributary. Radar estimates indicate that between 2.5 and 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
